differences.place: Line 6, initial darkened letters of multiombre
differences.evidence: The crop shows two superposed low, undulating runs at the start and then the clean l/t of multi. An earlier om is plausible, but the strokes do not distinguish an abandoned start from retracing the live beginning. The deletion state itself is therefore left open, rather than treating dark ink as a certain cancellation.

The accent is visible above the end of the long flattened final run. There is no separately recoverable terminal e after it, which favours formé; the flattened run could still absorb an additional e. Grammatical gender is not used to supply one.

differences.place: Line 9, replacement inclusion over the canceled start
differences.evidence: The live suffix sion is separable to the right, and the remaining overlap is consistent with inclusion. The initial letters cannot all be isolated from the cancellation; lexical uncertainty is retained. The insertion macro records the overwrite already indicated by H’s add and by C’s canceled-start context; that macro choice is not counted as an additional disagreement with C.

The final detached horizontal-returning run has a downturned end that can be a terminal s, favouring incidences. Because c/e/s are strongly compressed in this hand, the crop does not conclusively separate the plural ending from singular ce.
Half b: the i has its upper dot, followed by e and a final baseline dot. No additional baseline stop separates i and e. The page abbreviation is ie.

The crop gives a looped d followed by one low continuous e-like terminal stroke. It does not supply the separate intervening contours required to transcribe dans. The same short d-plus-flat-tail shape occurs in ordinary de elsewhere on this page.

The d is separate and clear; the following shallow cup with one terminal return is read as the writer’s flattened e. The word is de. The adjacent relation sign has both < and a lower stroke, and the next letter is a two-peaked cursive M.

The first letter is an open c with a descending returning cedilla, followed by a low a. The verb has the sequence of low runs and dotted i ending in a clear crossed t; it reads revient. H’s se réduisant is not supported by these strokes.

The upper mark is a separate almost straight bar. The lower mark begins with a bowl, rises sharply to an internal hump, and then continues in a long low tail; it is a flattened handwritten m, rather than a second straight equality stroke. The verbal abbreviation is preserved as a barred m.

Half b: two short separate words precede réconstitue; the reflexive se is visible, and the final word ends with the short tue sequence. There is no reconstituable ending. The clause is followed by pratiquement jamais.
Half b: the next line opens with the short reflexive se and then réconstitue. Its concluding t/u/e strokes agree with the first occurrence; neither est nor the able ending is present.

Half b: initial descending p, the medial crossed t and terminal t provide a readable pourtant despite local retracing. The C doubt is removed without inventing deleted letters beneath the darker strokes.

differences.place: Line 17, overwritten initial of souvent and live word
differences.evidence: The readable live continuation is ouvent, with the clear final tall t-like return, so the word is souvent. Only its first letter is densely overwritten. The old cluster has a rounded base, an upright and a short detached/oblique upper stroke: à and d remain possible; a complete canceled donc is not legible there. The replacement s is encoded at the overwritten position. Confidence in souvent is high; confidence in the canceled character is low.

The capital A has an extra small closed lower loop and doubled uprights. These are compatible with a lower-case a underneath, but they could also be a retraced/flourished capital A. No independent crossing line establishes cancellation. The alternatives retain uncertainty about the physical state, not the readable name Ateliers.

The crop separates the old tall d-like stroke and a small e-loop to its right from the newly rounded a and grave above. Thus de→à is the supported replacement; the old word is not another à. The live à is clear.

The sign has two linked returns with a long lower descending exit, supporting a section sign rather than S. The apparent crosswise portion belongs to that shape; no separate strike-through is visible. It is transcribed as live.

differences.place: Lines 3–4, quotation-mark form around de la figure
differences.evidence: Half a shows paired short upper strokes at the opening and closing, not angular guillemets. The literal double quotation marks are preserved. H’s emphasis macro and C’s underline macro describe the same single underline and are not separately collated.

differences.place: Line 18, quotation-mark form around Ateliers ensemblistes
differences.evidence: The opening marks are two short strokes, visible at the left of the crop, and the closing pair was read in half b. They are ordinary double quotation marks rather than guillemets. This row records glyph shape only, independently of the uncertain overwritten A.

content: The page says that the shadow of a figure consists of places refining it; these are called the places “of the figure”, with an explicit warning not to confuse them with its strata that are places.

The multi-shadow consists of the shadows of the strata, indexed by the deployment tilde F, the set of strata of F. The inclusion relation of the set-theoretic figure is identified with incidence between strata and with the relation on tilde F induced by ≤ on M.
The parenthetical statement says that using ≪ instead makes no difference: “ça revient au barred m”.
A figure is said almost never to reconstruct from its shadow but often to reconstruct from its multi-shadow, in the case of “Ateliers ensemblistes”. The author promises: “Nous y reviendrons.”
The final unfinished paragraph introduces “les relations d’ordre canoniques”.
math_reading_decisions: Read tilde, not a bar, above both relevant F’s; the tilde is a separate clear wave. Ordinary F remains distinct from cursive M.
The first order sign is ≤, with a distinct lower stroke; the second is ≪, two left-facing chevrons. Neither sign is an arrow.
Read de before tilde F and before M, rather than expanding to H’s dans. This is a literal prose decision and does not alter the intended induced-relation description.
Keep the written spelling déployement and uncertainty between incidences and incidence. No grammatical or mathematical normalization is made.
The sign after au is a barred verbal m. Its probable expansion is même, recorded only in abbreviations; it is not typeset as an equality sign.

The equivalence of the two induced relations and the reconstruction assertions were read as claims of the author. Their validity cannot be independently established from this isolated page, and no proof or counterexample was attempted.
author_doubts: No explicit question, doubt, “à vérifier”, or proof-check instruction occurs on the page.
“ça revient au barred m” is an equivalence assertion, not a doubt marker.
“Nous y reviendrons.” is a promise of later discussion, not a verification performed here.
